topic: Risk assessment documentation in mental health

audits.title: Assessing the quality of risk assessment conducted for new psychiatry inpatients
audits.standard: Documented risk assessment (risk to self, others, property) in junior doctor admission clerking
audits.setting: Two acute mental health wards (male and female)

cycle1.result: 12/30 (40%) had a junior doctor risk assessment in the clerking; 14 (47%) had no mention of risk on admission.

audits.other_findings: Of 12 assessments all covered self-harm and violence, but only 1 absconding. Teaching and a risk assessment template introduced, with re-audit under way.
audits.citation: Handa N. Assessing the quality of risk assessment conducted for new psychiatry inpatients. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S80-S80. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.251.

audits.title: Risk Assessments of Patients Admitted to Mixed Inpatient Psychiatric Wards: A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: Acute care group standard: patients with known risk to the opposite sex not admitted to mixed-sex wards; comprehensive risk assessment on admission with escalation to MDT
audits.setting: Mixed-sex inpatient psychiatric wards, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust

cycle1.result: Full risk assessment documented in 50%; historical risks in 40%; clerkings contained a risk assessment in 70%; 30% had risks to the opposite sex, none escalated to MDT

audits.other_findings: Recommended specific guidance and teaching; re-audit scheduled for March 2022.
audits.citation: Bennett S, Delaffon V. Risk Assessments of Patients Admitted to Mixed Inpatient Psychiatric Wards: A Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S150-S151. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.429.

audits.title: Use of Formulation Information Risk Management in Low Secure Services: An Audit Project
audits.standard: Trust standards for completion of the Formulation Information Risk Management (FIRM) assessment
audits.setting: Low secure services unit, Northern England, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Current/historical risks 100%; formulation 89%; Staying Safe/Staying Well care plan 73%; service user involved 16%; updated since last CPA 70%.

audits.intervention: Findings presented at local academic meeting and distributed to staff
audits.other_findings: Formulation and care plan completion improved compared with earlier auditing in October 2021 (figures not reported). Patient involvement was low, often because FIRM was completed at night.
audits.citation: Burns A. Use of Formulation Information Risk Management in Low Secure Services: An Audit Project. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S151-S152. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.431.

audits.title: Documentation Gaps in Suicide Risk Assessments: A Resident-Level Clinical Audit Using the C-SSRS Standard
audits.standard: C-SSRS: documentation of ideation, behaviour and use of a structured tool 100%; risk level and safety planning 90%
audits.setting: Department of psychiatry, Faisalabad Medical University (residents' records)

cycle1.result: Suicidal ideation documented 79.7%; behaviour 47.5%; intensity or frequency 25.4%; C-SSRS used 0.8%; risk level 2.5%; protective factors 0.8%; safety plan 0.8%.

audits.other_findings: Poor documentation was consistent across all residency levels. Recommended resident training and building C-SSRS into electronic records.
audits.citation: ALI I, Dogar I, Mustafa H, Asgher A, Zahra F. Documentation Gaps in Suicide Risk Assessments: A Resident-Level Clinical Audit Using the C-SSRS Standard. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S272-S273. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11569.

audits.title: Improving Compliance With Annual Structured Risk Assessment in an Older Adult Community Mental Health Team: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit
audits.standard: Local guidance: CRAFT risk assessment updated at least annually, or sooner if risk changes
audits.setting: Older adult community mental health team, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde (Gartnavel Royal Hospital)

cycle1.period: 16 December 2024 to 14 March 2025 (medical); mid-February to mid-March 2025 (nurse-led)

audits.intervention: Findings presented at the community MDT meeting and email to clinicians with updated guidance on CRAFT completion and how to find the date of the last CRAFT.

cycle2.period: Mid-April to mid-July 2025 (medical); mid-June to mid-July 2025 (nurse-led)

audits.other_findings: Time pressure in medical clinics and lack of automated EMIS prompts were likely causes; electronic prompts suggested.
audits.citation: Farooq M. Improving Compliance With Annual Structured Risk Assessment in an Older Adult Community Mental Health Team: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S292-S293. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11721.

audits.title: Audit of Completion of Risk Assessment on Admission & Discharge - Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore
audits.standard: Risk assessment within 24 hours of admission covering all risk domains, risk management plan, and review and update before discharge
audits.setting: Psychiatry inpatient unit, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore

cycle1.result: Admission risk assessment within 24 hours 64%; documentation in notes 84%; risk from others 68%; risk management plan 72%; review before discharge 40%; update before discharge 40%.

audits.intervention: Staff education, risk-assessment checklists displayed on the ward, and ward-round reminders.

cycle2.result: Admission risk assessment within 24 hours 92%; documentation 96%; risk from others 88%; risk management plan 88%; review before discharge 84%; update before discharge 80%.

audits.other_findings: Audit ran over two months. Standardised admission and discharge proformas are recommended.
audits.citation: Siraj S, Ijaz M, Ali M, Jannat S, Siraj S. Audit of Completion of Risk Assessment on Admission & Discharge - Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S344-S345. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11840.
